_readme: Behavioural and fit questions for the interview tab (DESIGN.md section 3).
This is DATA, not code (CLAUDE.md rule 4): add firms, groups or questions here, never in lib/.
These are questions commonly asked in MBB fit and behavioural rounds, compiled from
widely published prep material and the firms' own stated values. They are NOT a leaked
script, and no firm asks all of them. `firms` marks where a question is especially
likely; `lookFor` says what a strong answer shows; a firm-specific note is advice
grounded in that firm's public values, not insider knowledge.
`competency` uses the same labels as lib/stories/types.ts DEFAULT_VOCAB where one
fits, so a written answer is indexed against the same gaps the rest of the tab shows.

questions.text: Walk me through your CV.
questions.lookFor: A two-minute story with a through-line, not a list of jobs. Each move should have a reason, and it should end pointing at this firm.
questions.bain: Almost always the opener. It sets the tone for the whole conversation, so rehearse the first sentence until it is automatic.

questions.text: Why consulting?
questions.lookFor: A reason rooted in something you have done, not a generic appeal to learning and variety. Specific beats enthusiastic.

questions.text: Why this firm, and not the others?
questions.lookFor: Something true about this firm that is not on its homepage, and ideally a person you have actually spoken to there.
questions.bain: Bain's stated values include candour, results over reports, and a team culture it describes as never letting a colleague fail. An answer that names one of these AND connects it to your own experience lands far better than praise.

questions.text: Why did you decide to do an MBA?
questions.lookFor: A real trigger and a real timing reason. A decision has a moment; a manufactured one does not, and interviewers press on exactly that.

questions.text: What did you learn during your MBA that will make you a better consultant?
questions.lookFor: One demonstrated change in how you work, shown through something you did - not a list of courses.

questions.text: What is a genuine development area for you?
questions.lookFor: A real weakness, evidence you have noticed it in action, and what you are concretely doing about it. Disguised strengths are spotted instantly.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you led a team through something difficult.
questions.lookFor: What made it difficult, what YOU did specifically, and how the team came out of it - not only the outcome.

questions.text: Describe a time you were part of a team that was not working well. What did you do?
questions.lookFor: Diagnosis of why it was not working, a personal intervention, and a changed dynamic.
questions.bain: Team orientation is central to how Bain describes itself. Expect this or a close variant, and expect a follow-up on how you supported someone else rather than yourself.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped a colleague succeed at your own expense.
questions.lookFor: A real cost to you, a clear benefit to them, and no hint of martyrdom.
questions.bain: This probes the 'never let a colleague fail' value directly. A strong answer shows the trade-off you made was deliberate.

questions.text: Tell me about working with someone very different from you.
questions.lookFor: Real difference in working style or view, what you adapted, and what you learned from them.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you persuaded someone senior who did not have to listen to you.
questions.lookFor: The objection they raised, how you reframed around what they cared about, and the moment they moved.

questions.text: Describe a time you got something done without formal authority.
questions.lookFor: Who you needed, why they had no reason to help, and what you did to earn it.

questions.text: Tell me about a serious disagreement with a colleague or manager.
questions.lookFor: A real disagreement, how you handled it directly and respectfully, and the outcome - including if you were wrong.
questions.bain: Bain names candour as a value. Expect a follow-up on whether you raised it directly, and with whom.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to deliver an unpopular message.
questions.lookFor: Why it had to be said, how you prepared, how it was received, and what happened next.
questions.bain: Directly tests candour. The best answers show you said it early rather than letting a problem grow.

questions.text: Walk me through a problem you solved with no clear structure or data.
questions.lookFor: How you created structure: the hypotheses you formed, how you tested them, and what you ruled out.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you used data to change a decision.
questions.lookFor: The decision before, the analysis, the specific insight, and the decision after - with the number that moved it.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had too much to do. How did you decide what mattered?
questions.lookFor: An explicit prioritisation logic, what you deliberately dropped, and who you told.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you understood a customer's problem better than they did.
questions.lookFor: What they asked for, what they actually needed, how you found the gap, and what changed.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you failed.
questions.lookFor: A genuine failure with real consequences, your share of the responsibility, and a specific change you made afterwards. A success in disguise is spotted instantly.

questions.text: Describe a time a plan you were responsible for went wrong.
questions.lookFor: How early you noticed, how you communicated it, and how you recovered.

questions.text: Tell me about the most difficult feedback you have received.
questions.lookFor: Feedback that stung, why it was fair, and evidence you acted on it.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you delivered under serious time pressure.
questions.lookFor: The real constraint, the trade-offs you made to meet it, and the quality of what shipped.

questions.text: What achievement are you most proud of, and why?
questions.lookFor: The why matters more than the what. It reveals what you value.
questions.bain: Bain's focus on results means the impact should be concrete - say the number.

questions.text: Tell me about something you started that nobody asked you to.
questions.lookFor: The gap you spotted, why you acted without permission, and the lasting result.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you changed your mind.
questions.lookFor: What you believed, what evidence moved you, and how quickly you acted on it.

questions.text: Tell me about a time your work made a measurable difference to a client or customer.
questions.lookFor: The client, the difference, and the number.
questions.bain: Maps directly onto Bain's 'results, not reports'. Lead with the outcome.
